body:
Sent the full latest package (mq4/ex4, forge_ledger.json, both ARGUS docs, plus the two real evidence logs) timestamped 2026-08-25T20-57-07Z.

ANSWER TO MY OWN QUESTION -- checked the real evidence instead of guessing:

TUNGSTEN_ratchet.log (only 3 entries ever, real data): July 23 -- ghostWR 0%, 0 OOS trades, 2/6 gates. Aug 6 -- ghostWR 100%, but only 1 OOS trade, 5/6 gates. Aug 13 -- ghostWR 0%, 0 OOS trades, 3/6 gates. Never once 6/6. Never once a real statistically-powered OOS sample.

TUNGSTEN_live.log's most recent run (Aug 24, USDJPY M5, real 90-min budget): Phase 1 (baseline signal quality) FAILED on first attempt -- 28.6% WR, "barely above random (29%) -- components not discriminative." It retried and moved on to Phase 2 (8 viable regimes learned), started Phase 3B, and the log just stops mid-regime-1-of-9. No ARMED file exists for any instrument, anywhere.

Straight answer: the Living-Edge "powered run" precondition is NOT met. Not close. TUNGSTEN has never completed a full calibration to a real promotion. This isn't a reason to feel bad about it -- it's the actual, honest current state, and it points at something more fundamental than "wire in Living-Edge": Phase 1 baseline signal quality is failing/barely-passing on real recent data, and full calibration runs aren't finishing within their time budget. That's a more load-bearing problem than the dead-code findings from earlier today.

Given that, I did NOT wire Living-Edge in -- doing so on zero real evidence would be exactly the kind of premature activation the system's own gate exists to prevent. The real next lever, if you want it, is digging into WHY Phase 1 keeps barely failing and why full runs aren't completing in the time budget -- that's calibration-root-cause work, not more dead-code hunting, and it's a different, deeper investigation than anything I've done today.

Want me to go there next?
